title: kith-peer: DeliverHandler does not check if contact is blocked before accepting delivery
description: DeliverHandler (kith-peer/src/lib.rs) accepts messages from any caller that passes the kithd auth layer (is_permitted returns true for non-blocked contacts). However, is_permitted in kith-store/src/contact.rs already returns false for blocked contacts, so the auth layer already gates on blocked status. The outbox worker checks blocked status explicitly. But the inbound DeliverHandler never reads the blocked flag itself — it relies entirely on is_permitted. This is currently correct because is_permitted checks \!blocked, but the fact that the handler comment (step 8 in the doc block) does not mention blocked-contact rejection, and there is no explicit test covering 'blocked peer delivers → 401/403', makes this an invisible invariant. If is_permitted ever changes to only check existence (not blocked status), blocked contacts could deliver messages without any code change catching the regression.
